title: Sephiria Scythe: Dagger → Drifa (Not a 6th Weapon)
description: How to get the scythe in Sephiria: Dagger → Dormant Frost → Drifa turns Blizzard Hammer into Blizzard Scythe. Not a sixth weapon branch.
h1: Sephiria Scythe: Dagger → Drifa (not a 6th weapon)
body:
Search intent check: “How to get the scythe in Sephiria” usually means the Blizzard Scythe weapon skill—not a seventh starter weapon. Official branch lists stop at six.

Blizzard Scythe path (Dagger)

  1. Play Dagger.
  2. At the Anvil, take the frost enhancement line Dormant Frost.
  3. Second enhancement Drifa converts Blizzard Hammer into Blizzard Scythe.

Korean clear videos build around Ice Armament + Precision, shop needles (Northbound Golden Needle), and Glacier support. Once Drifa lands, dash-fired scythes become the carry.

What has to be true before Drifa can appear

Dagger has to be unlocked first. The weapons page records the unlock route for a branch: progress to the chapter that opens weapon training, buy the weapon training node on Destiny Inscription with Sapphires, then finish the short training ground with the village NPC and the weapon appears on the village rack. The characters page names that NPC — Moro, written Morrow in some guides, on the east side of the training ground — and lists Dagger among the branches that route opens.

The two enhancement steps are offers, not purchases. The same weapons page records that upgrades come from what the run shows you, that each branch draws from a pool advertised at more than 50 unique upgrades, and that community 1.0 data reports Greatsword upgrades appearing more often than Dagger upgrades. That last point is the real cost of a scythe attempt: the route needs two specific Dagger offers, in order, before the conversion can happen at all. A run that reaches the Anvil and is offered nothing on the frost line is not unlucky in a vague way; it is on a branch whose offers are reported as thinner.

This is also why the beginner guide says to prefer the Anvil early. Weapon skill offers are what let a forced build exist, and a scythe run is the clearest example of a build that has to be forced.

Where the run commits

Two enhancement slots are the whole budget for the weapon line in the sources cited here. Dormant Frost takes the first, Drifa takes the second, and the conversion happens on the second. By the time the scythe exists there is nothing left to spend on a different weapon idea in that run, which is what “committed” means on this page.

If Drifa never appears, the run is still a frost-oriented Dagger. Whether that is acceptable depends on the rest of the plan and on what the pool offers next, and this page cannot tell you which offer will arrive first. The practical read is that a scythe run should be started when you are willing to play a Dagger run either way, not as a coin flip you only accept one outcome of.

Not the same item

Verut’s Scythe can drop as an Artifact tied to execution/crit fantasies. Do not confuse it with the Drifa weapon conversion.

The two are different categories of thing. One is a weapon skill that only exists inside a Dagger run that reached Drifa; the other is an Artifact that can appear as a drop and belongs on the inventory grid described on the Artifacts page. A search that mixes them produces advice that cannot be followed, such as farming for a weapon that is not a drop.

The conversion path, step by step

StepWhat you doWhat changes
1Start a run on the Dagger branchYou are on one of the six official weapon branches; there is no seventh starter
2At the Anvil, take the frost enhancement line, Dormant FrostThe weapon keeps the Dagger branch identity but gains the cold line
3Take the second enhancement, DrifaBlizzard Hammer converts into Blizzard Scythe — this is the scythe people search for

The path is short; the cost is that both enhancement slots are spent on the frost line, so the run is committed to it by the time Drifa appears. Source: the branch listing and 1.0 play notes already cited on this page.

Which frost route you are actually on

Dagger has two documented frost routes, and they are easy to conflate because both start on the same branch and both use cold. The difference is the first enhancement, so the choice is made earlier than it feels:

RouteSteps as the community writes themWhat the record says you get
Blizzard ScytheDagger, then Dormant Frost, then DrifaBlizzard Hammer converts into Blizzard Scythe
Frozen SmeltDagger, then Sleeping Frost, then Frozen SmeltA named endpoint on the Dagger frost line; the record gives the name and the steps, not the effect

Both routes are listed on the weapons page from community reporting at 1.0.x. Dormant Frost and Sleeping Frost are separate entries, not two names for one step — so a run follows one line or the other. Nothing on this site documents taking both in a single run, and no page here publishes a damage comparison between the two endpoints.

That gap matters for planning. The scythe route is chosen for the conversion itself — the weapon becomes a different skill — while Frozen Smelt is recorded only as a named evolution. If what you want is a specific end state you have seen in a video, match the video to one of these two lines before you start, because as far as these records go the first frost offer is where they diverge.

When the scythe is worth taking over the alternatives

The comparison below is an editorial read of the branch tradeoffs on the weapons page, not a ranking and not a damage table. No page on this site publishes scythe damage numbers, cooldowns or scaling, so nothing here should be read as “the scythe is stronger”.

AlternativeWhat that option gives youWhen the scythe route still makes sense
Frozen Smelt, same branchThe other documented frost endpoint on DaggerWhen the conversion into a scythe skill is the thing you want, rather than a named evolution
KatanaAggressive melee with a high ceiling once parry timing is learned, and a steeper mastery curveWhen you already defend by reacting and dashing rather than by holding block
Sword and ShieldDefensive close melee, the usual pick for first runs and pattern learningOnce the fights are known and the block is no longer the plan
CrossbowRanged positioning, kiting and safe damage, at the cost of reload disciplineRarely, in the sense that a scythe run is a melee commitment on a branch whose listed tradeoff is extremely short reach

Branch tradeoffs from the six-branch table on the weapons page; the “when it still makes sense” column is our reading, not a game fact.

The support pieces carry as much weight as the conversion. The reports cited above pair the scythe with Ice Armament and Precision, Glacier-tagged support, and shop-bought needles. If those never show up, Drifa alone leaves you holding a converted weapon on a thin board — the risk any plan that hangs on a single arrival carries.

One tag is worth watching because it does double duty. Ice Armament appears in the bond table on the Artifacts page as half of Droplet of Plitvice, with Lake as the other half. If a run is already carrying Ice Armament for the scythe plan, that bond needs only Lake on top of what the board already has instead of two new tags — and if it does not appear, nothing in the weapon plan breaks.

Why searches for “Sephiria scythe” mislead

Two different things get called a scythe: the Blizzard Scythe weapon skill above, and a rumoured seventh weapon branch. The store listing and every official branch summary stop at six families — Sword and Shield, Greatsword, Dagger, Crossbow, Katana, Staff/Quarterstaff — so a “scythe branch” does not exist in 1.0. If a video shows a scythe, the most likely explanation is a Dagger run that reached Drifa; the branch list itself has no scythe entry.

That distinction matters when you plan: you cannot start as a scythe user, so the first two floors decide whether the run happens at all. Build the Dagger plan first, then decide whether the frost commitment is worth it.

What this page cannot confirm

  • Current labels. The builds page keeps this route as a legacy community report and asks you to verify the evolution names and unlocks in your Journal. The same applies here.
  • Offer order. Whether Dormant Frost and then Drifa appear in a given run depends on the branch pool the weapons page describes; no page here promises the sequence.
  • Numbers. No damage, cooldown, scaling or drop-rate figure for Blizzard Scythe appears on this page, because none is published in the sources cited.
  • Verut’s Scythe conditions. The record says it can drop as an Artifact tied to execution/crit fantasies. It does not give a source, a rate, or a floor.
  • A scythe branch. The branch summaries stop at six, so there is no seventh starter to unlock, whatever a search result suggests.
  • Scythe against Frozen Smelt in practice. Both are recorded as frost endpoints, and no comparison between them is published here.

Quick FAQ

Is the scythe a seventh weapon?

No. Official branch summaries stop at six families in 1.0. The scythe is a Dagger conversion reached through Dormant Frost and Drifa.

Do I need Dagger unlocked first?

Yes. The weapons page route is a Destiny Inscription weapon training node plus the training ground with the village NPC, and Dagger is listed among the branches that route opens.

Can the scythe drop instead?

Not as described here. The page records Blizzard Scythe as a weapon conversion. The scythe that appears as a drop is Verut’s Scythe, which is an Artifact.

Does Drifa always show up?

There is no guarantee on this page. Upgrades are offers drawn from a branch pool, and community data already reports Dagger offers appearing less often than Greatsword offers.

How many enhancement steps does it take?

Two: Dormant Frost, then Drifa. Both slots are spent on the frost line, which is why the run is committed by the time the scythe exists.

Should I plan the whole run around it?

Plan the Dagger run first and treat the conversion as the outcome you want, not the only acceptable one. If Drifa does not arrive, you are still playing a frost-oriented Dagger.
